explanation: Gregor Mendel was an Austrian monk who studied science and mathematics at the University of Vienna. He performed controlled breeding experiments with the garden pea, Pisum sativum, carefully collecting and documenting quantitative, mathematical data. Based on these experiments, he formulated the fundamental laws of heredity in the early 1860s. Remarkably, he did this without any knowledge of chromosomes or cells, and without the aid of a microscope.
